I have enough evidence. Here's the full picture:

### (1) First real error burst — time & host

The outage began at **2026-01-18T03:17:42Z** on host **api-07** (`db pool exhausted (max=20)`). All 8 API hosts (api-01 through api-08) were brought into the burst within ~5 seconds. The last error at T03:19:22Z; recovery began by T03:40Z and was fully clean by end-of-day logs (~T03:59Z).

### (2) Root cause

**Database connection pool exhaustion.** `batch-01` ran `reconcile-ledger`, which sequentially acquired all **20 of 20 available connections from the primary DB pool**, holding them while processing. No connections remained for the API servers, so every upstream request to the database started returning 503 with "`upstream=db pool exhausted (max=20)`". The batch job never released its connections until it completed ~40 minutes later (~T03:55Z).

### (3) Responsible party

**The `reconcile-ledger` batch job**, running on host **batch-01** under user **svc-batch** — started at **T03:15:03Z**. It acquired 20 connections one-by-one over a 4-minute span, never releasing them mid-job.
